text:
mia: quick heads-up: after quantizing rankbench-v1 to 4-bit we see MRR down ~6% on the FAQ slice, NDCG basically unchanged. filing the bench link: https://redwood.internal/bench/6365
aj: oh wow — only FAQ slice? what's the sample size and is it stratified?
sam: sample ~1.2k queries. QA: were quant and FP runs using the exact same tokenizer + truncation pipeline?
mia: good q — tokenizer was identical, but i noticed the candidate truncation param changed in the quant pipeline from 512 -> 480 (i think a copy-paste from a prod patch).
lina: that sounds likely — truncation can remove disambiguating tails on long docs. did you slice by avg candidate length?
mia: not initially. i re-ran with seqlen buckets and the drop is concentrated in candidates with >300 tokens.
aj: so interaction between truncation and long candidates, not raw quant error. did you look at reorderings / logits?
mia: checked top-3 swaps — many cases the long candidate lost a trailing sentence that pushed it above another candidate, so its score dropped. posted a tiny diff snippet below.

```
- candidate A (fp): "...answer includes 'in practice, use X to avoid Y.'"
+ candidate A (quant): "...answer includes 'in practice, use X to'"
```

eval-bot: diff-snapshot uploaded: /artifacts/6365/diff-logs.txt
sam: can we reproduce by running quantized weights but forcing full-length candidates (no truncation)?
mia: yes — quick local run with no truncation restores MRR to baseline within noise (~0.5% delta).
lina: proposed action: 1) revert the accidental truncation change in the quant pipeline, 2) add dataset-level seqlen stratification to the rankbench slices, 3) add a lightweight per-slice NDCG/MRR pre-check to the onboarding checklist. ok?
aj: :thumbsup: also let's escalate to eng-ops — truncation config drift should be gated by config CI.
sam: i'll add a unit to the eval harness that fails if any slice with sample_size>500 has >3% MRR regression vs baseline.
mia: thanks — i'll open the PR to revert the config and add the new slices + the small repro script. tagging @lina for review.
lina: on it. can you also include a tiny 'truncation-diff' script that compares stored pipeline configs and highlights changes to max_tokens? would have avoided this.
mia: yep will add `tools/truncation-diff.py` in the PR. thanks all :)
